title: God’s work cannot be frustrated, but Joseph can still fall
setting: From April to June 1828, Joseph Smith dictated the first Book of Mormon manuscript at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Martin Harris as scribe. Harris pressed to take the 116 pages home to Palmyra, New York, and Joseph finally agreed. Soon after, Emma Smith gave birth to a son who did not survive, and Joseph cared for her for weeks. In early July he went to Palmyra and learned the pages were lost. Joseph’s history says he received this revelation through the Urim and Thummim after returning to Harmony. It is the earliest of his revelations with a surviving text.
summary: The revelation begins by declaring that God’s works and purposes cannot be frustrated. It is the work of men that fails, especially those who boast in their own strength. It then turns to Joseph and recalls how strict his commandments were. It says he gave in to the persuasions of men and feared man more than God. If Joseph repents, he is still chosen; if not, he will lose his gift. He lost his privileges for handing sacred things to a wicked man. Still, the revelation says, the work will go forth. It says the plates were preserved so the Lamanites might know the promises made to their fathers and believe in Christ.

contextNote.title: Whose work failed
contextNote.text: The lost pages could look like a failure of God’s plan. Verse 3 says the failure belongs to “the work of men,” not to the work of God. Verse 4 describes how a man falls, through boasting and following his own will. Verses 6–7 say Joseph had “gone on in the persuasions of men” and feared man more than God. Verse 10 keeps the door open: if he repents, he is “still chosen” for the work. Verse 16 then repeats the opening claim that “my work shall go forth” despite the loss. In this revelation, frustrated work belongs to people who stop following God’s counsel, not to God.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 draws from this section the teaching that we can trust God. According to verses 7–8, what would God have done for Joseph if he had stayed faithful under pressure?
reviewNote: Read all 20 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, July 1828, after the 116 pages were lost, received through the Urim and Thummim. JSP historical introduction read for the April–June dictation, Harris’s request, the 15 June birth and death of Emma’s son, the early-July trip to Palmyra, and the status as the first revelation with a surviving text. The 116-page figure is from the official heading. How the text was first written down is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote said verse 4 describes how a man’s work fails; verse 4 describes how a man falls. Summary sentence on the plates’ purpose now attributed to the text.
